problem: A hot air balloon that is launched vertically is observed by a child located on the ground $4\,\text{km}$ from the launch site. What is the vertical speed of the balloon at the instant when its distance from the child is $5\,\text{km}$ and this distance is increasing at a rate of $12\,\text{km/h}?$
worked_solution:
We start by drawing a diagram of the problem.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14066033/assets/40957ce27304474263d1d231a3a0df93193ac0461d8a7444cde3b12047d1a214.png)

In the diagram,

- $x$ is the distance between the child and the launch site,

- $y$ is the distance between the launch site and the balloon,

- $z$ is the distance between the child and the balloon.

As shown in the diagram, $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ form a right triangle with $z$ as the hypotenuse. We wish to find the rate of change of $y,$ which is $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$ 

We know that $z=5\,\text{km}$ and $x=4\,\text{km}.$ We can find $y$ using the Pythagorean Theorem, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ {4}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={5}^{2} \\ {y}^{2} & =9 \\ y & =3\,\text{km}\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that:

- $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}=12\,\text{km}/\text{h},$

- the distance between the child and the launch site ($x$) remains the same, so $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=0.$

Finally, we differentiate both sides of ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={z}^{2}$ with respect to $t$ and then substitute in the known values, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({z}^{2}) \\ 2x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ 2(4)(0)+2(3)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2(5)(12) \\ 6\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =120 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{120}{6} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertical speed of the hot air balloon is $20\,\text{km}/\text{h}.$
